summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant presented for elective repair of a symptomatic right inguinal hernia. He underwent an open Bassini repair without complications. Postoperatively, he experienced moderate pain requiring tramadol, which led to an overnight stay for pain management. By the next morning, his pain was well controlled, he was ambulating independently, and his incision was clean and dry. He was discharged home with instructions on wound care, activity restrictions, and medication changes, including a switch from sirolimus to tacrolimus and the addition of ferrous sulfate for anemia. Follow-up was arranged with the transplant and surgical teams.
problems: Inguinal hernia, without mention of obstruction or gangrene, unilateral or unspecified (not specified as recurrent)
